outcomes.resolution_summary: Kubernetes 1.24 shipped with dockershim removed from kubelet, requiring a CRI-compatible runtime or an external adapter for Docker Engine.

cruxes.description: Whether Kubernetes maintainers would follow through on the announced 1.24 removal schedule rather than postpone it again.
Whether containerd, CRI-O, or cri-dockerd provided a viable migration target before Kubernetes 1.24.
Whether node tooling and workloads depended on Docker Engine behavior beyond the kubelet integration.

outcomes.resolution_summary: The Python Steering Council accepted PEP 703 with a gradual, reversible rollout, targeting an optional no-GIL build for Python 3.13.

cruxes.description: Whether the Steering Council would accept the implementation risk if rollout could remain optional and reversible.
Whether the proposal's single-threaded performance cost was small enough for a gradual CPython roadmap.
Whether the C-extension ecosystem could transition without making the proposal operationally untenable.

outcomes.resolution_summary: The official Node.js schedule retained 2023-09-11 as the Node.js 16 end-of-life date; the line was not extended beyond that date.

authoritative_sources.title: Node.js release schedule after Node.js 16 end-of-life

cruxes.description: Whether OpenSSL 1.1.1 support constraints made the accelerated Node.js 16 end date difficult to extend.
Whether Node.js release governance would preserve the revised date after publicly updating the schedule.
Whether a supported successor LTS line was available early enough to make migration practical.

outcomes.resolution_summary: Python 3.12 removed distutils from the standard library and directed projects that still needed it to install setuptools separately.

cruxes.description: Whether setuptools and maintained packaging interfaces covered the practical distutils migration path.
Whether CPython could remove its own build-time dependence on distutils before Python 3.12.
Whether downstream packages could update imports before removal without prohibitive disruption.
